newsitem.title: USA: U.S. union chief urges members to work election.
newsitem.headline: U.S. union chief urges members to work election.

text.p: AFL-CIO President John Sweeney, calling Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole the "Darth Vader of American politics," urged workers Tuesday to get out and work for President Clinton and unseat the Republican Congress.

"Two years ago we lost 29 Congressional districts to 'Newtie and the Blowhards' by less than 5,000 votes," Sweeney told members of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, referring to House Speaker Newt Gingrich and the Republican freshmen in Congress as a "gangsta rap group."
"In those districts (where Republicans won) we had two to three times that many union members who didn't even vote," Sweeney said.

Sweeney, who oversees 13 million members of affiliated American unions, including the 477,000 machinists, said the AFL-CIO hoped to put at least "100 activists" in each congressional district and counted on 30 hours of electioneering work from each before election day Nov. 5.
"You have to work together with other members in your lodge and with the people in your community like serious voters and get involved in this dirty business called politics," he said.
The AFL-CIO has also spent millions of dollars on television ads critical of conservative Republicans and Dole.

"He's still the Darth Vader of American politics and his record is clear," Sweeney said, comparing Dole to the evil commander in the "Star Wars" movie trilogy. "Well, I have bad news for Candidate Dole. You've been an anti-worker, anti-union politician for 40 years and we're not going to forget."

Later, delegates to the union's annual convention cheered House Minority Leader, Missouri Democrat Richard Gephardt, chanting "speaker, speaker" in hopes of a return to Democratic control of Congress which would likely make Gephardt Speaker of the House.
